title: अध्याय १००

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
तस्य सन्ताप्यमाने तु तेजसोर्ध्वमधस्यथा ।
सिसृक्षुश्चिन्तयामास पद्मयोनिः पितामहः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
tasya santāpyamāne tu tejasordhvamadhasyathā |
sisṛkṣuścintayāmāsa padmayoniḥ pitāmahaḥ || 1 ||

items.text:
सृष्टिः कृतापि मे नाशं प्रयास्यत्यभितेजसा ।
भास्वतः सृष्टिसंहारस्थितिहेतोर्महात्मनः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
sṛṣṭiḥ kṛtāpi me nāśaṃ prayāsyatyabhitejasā |
bhāsvataḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārasthitihetormahātmanaḥ || 2 ||

items.text:
अप्राणाः प्राणिनः सर्व आपः शुष्यन्ति तेजसा ।
न चाम्भसा विना सृष्टिर्विश्वस्यास्य भविष्यति ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
aprāṇāḥ prāṇinaḥ sarva āpaḥ śuṣyanti tejasā |
na cāmbhasā vinā sṛṣṭirviśvasyāsya bhaviṣyati || 3 ||

items.text:
इति सञ्चिन्त्य भगवान्स्तोत्रं भगवतो रवेः ।
चकार तन्मये भूत्वा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
iti sañcintya bhagavānstotraṃ bhagavato raveḥ |
cakāra tanmaye bhūtvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नमस्ये यन्मयं सर्वमेतत्सर्वमयश्च यः ।
विश्वमूर्तिः परं ज्योतिर्यत्तद्ध्यायन्ति योगिनः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
brahmovāca
namasye yanmayaṃ sarvametatsarvamayaśca yaḥ |
viśvamūrtiḥ paraṃ jyotiryattaddhyāyanti yoginaḥ || 5 ||

items.text:
य ऋङ्मयो यो यजुषां निधानं साम्नां च यो योनिरचिन्त्यशक्तिः ।
त्रयीमयः स्थूलतयार्धमात्रा परस्वरूपो गुणपारयोग्यः ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
ya ṛṅmayo yo yajuṣāṃ nidhānaṃ sāmnāṃ ca yo yoniracintyaśaktiḥ |
trayīmayaḥ sthūlatayārdhamātrā parasvarūpo guṇapārayogyaḥ || 6 ||

items.text:
त्वां सर्वहेतुं परमं च वेद्यमाद्यं परं ज्योतिरवेद्यरूपम् ।
स्थूलं च देवात्मतया नमस्ते भास्वन्तमाद्यं परमं परेभ्यः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
tvāṃ sarvahetuṃ paramaṃ ca vedyamādyaṃ paraṃ jyotiravedyarūpam |
sthūlaṃ ca devātmatayā namaste bhāsvantamādyaṃ paramaṃ parebhyaḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
सृष्टिं करोमि यदहं तव शक्तिराद्या तत्प्रेरितो जलमहीपवनाग्निरूपाम् ।
तद्देवतादिविषयां प्रणवाद्यशेषां नात्मेच्छया स्थितिलयावपि तद्वदेव ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
sṛṣṭiṃ karomi yadahaṃ tava śaktirādyā tatprerito jalamahīpavanāgnirūpām |
taddevatādiviṣayāṃ praṇavādyaśeṣāṃ nātmecchayā sthitilayāvapi tadvadeva || 8 ||

items.text:
वह्निस्त्वमेव जलशोषणतः पृथिव्याः सृष्टिं करोषि जगतां च तथाद्य पाकम् ।
व्यापी त्वमेव भगवन्गगनस्वरूपं त्वं पञ्चधा जगदिदं परिपासि विश्वम् ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
vahnistvameva jalaśoṣaṇataḥ pṛthivyāḥ sṛṣṭiṃ karoṣi jagatāṃ ca tathādya pākam |
vyāpī tvameva bhagavangaganasvarūpaṃ tvaṃ pañcadhā jagadidaṃ paripāsi viśvam || 9 ||

items.text:
यज्ञैर्यजन्ति परमात्मविदो भवन्तं विष्णुस्वरूपमखिलेष्टिमयं विवस्वन् ।
ध्यायन्ति चापि यतयो नियतात्मचित्ताः सर्वेश्वरं परममात्मविमुक्तिकामा ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
yajñairyajanti paramātmavido bhavantaṃ viṣṇusvarūpamakhileṣṭimayaṃ vivasvan |
dhyāyanti cāpi yatayo niyatātmacittāḥ sarveśvaraṃ paramamātmavimuktikāmā || 10 ||

items.text:
नमस्ते देवरूपाय यज्ञरूपाय ते नमः ।
परब्रह्मस्वरूपाय चिन्त्यमानाय योगिभिः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
namaste devarūpāya yajñarūpāya te namaḥ |
parabrahmasvarūpāya cintyamānāya yogibhiḥ || 11 ||

items.text:
उपसंहर तेजो यत्तेजसः संहतिस्तव ।
सृष्टेर्विधाताय विभो सृष्टौ चाहं समुद्यतः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
upasaṃhara tejo yattejasaḥ saṃhatistava |
sṛṣṭervidhātāya vibho sṛṣṭau cāhaṃ samudyataḥ || 12 ||

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
इत्येवं संस्तुतो भास्वान्ब्रह्मणा सर्गकर्तृणा ।
उपसंहृतवांस्तेजः परं स्वल्पमधारयत् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
ityevaṃ saṃstuto bhāsvānbrahmaṇā sargakartṛṇā |
upasaṃhṛtavāṃstejaḥ paraṃ svalpamadhārayat || 13 ||

items.text:
चकार च ततः सृष्टिं जगतः पद्मसम्भवः ।
तथा तेषु महाभागः पूर्वकल्पान्तरेषु वै ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
cakāra ca tataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ jagataḥ padmasambhavaḥ |
tathā teṣu mahābhāgaḥ pūrvakalpāntareṣu vai || 14 ||

items.text:
देवासुरादीन्मर्त्त्यांश्च पश्वादीन्वृक्षवीरुधः ।
ससर्ज पूर्ववद्ब्रह्मा नरकांश्च महामुने ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
devāsurādīnmarttyāṃśca paśvādīnvṛkṣavīrudhaḥ |
sasarja pūrvavadbrahmā narakāṃśca mahāmune || 15 ||

en_summary: Markandeya continues. As the Sun's light burned above and below, Brahma, born from the lotus, wishing to create, worried: the creation he made would be destroyed by the great heat of the Sun, the cause of creation, preservation and destruction; living beings would lose their breath and the waters would dry up, and without water there could be no creation. So Brahma, grandfather of the worlds, became absorbed in the Sun and sang a hymn to him. He bows to the one of whom all this is made and who is made of all, whose form is the universe, the supreme light on which yogis meditate; who is made of the Rig, the store of the Yajus and the source of the Saman, of unthinkable power, made of the three Vedas, the half-syllable (of Om) in gross form, the supreme form fit to go beyond the qualities; the cause of all, the highest to be known, the first, the supreme light whose form cannot be known, and gross as the self of the gods. Brahma says that when he creates, it is the Sun's first power, urged by him, that creates the world in the form of water, earth, wind and fire, with its gods, objects and all that begins with Om; it is not by Brahma's own will, and the same is true of preservation and dissolution. The Sun is fire; by drying the water he creates the earth and he cooks the worlds; he is the all-pervading sky; in five forms he protects this universe. Those who know the Supreme Self worship him with sacrifices as Vishnu, made of all offerings, and self-controlled ascetics who seek liberation meditate on him as the lord of all. Bowing to him as the form of the gods, of sacrifice and of the supreme Brahman, on whom yogis meditate, Brahma asks him to draw in his light, since Brahma is ready to create. So praised by Brahma the creator, the Sun drew in his light and kept only a little. Then Brahma created the world as in earlier kalpas: gods, asuras and others, humans, animals and others, trees and creepers, and also the hells.
